description: Seed problems for Karnaugh Map Minimization and Quine-McCluskey Optimization

problems.title: Essential prime implicants only: F = BD
problems.statement: Minimize the 4-variable function F(A,B,C,D) = Σm(5, 7, 13, 15) using a Karnaugh map.

steps.prompt: Identify the maximal group covering all minterms {5, 7, 13, 15}.

explanation: Minterms m5 (0101), m7 (0111), m13 (1101), and m15 (1111) form a contiguous 2x2 square in columns CD=01, 11 across rows AB=01, 11. The common literals are B=1 and D=1, giving BD as the single essential prime implicant.
problems.learningObjective: Form a maximal rectangular group of size 4 on a 4-variable K-map and extract the minimal product term.

problems.title: Four-corner wrap-around grouping: F = B'D'
problems.statement: Find the minimal SOP expression for F(A,B,C,D) = Σm(0, 2, 8, 10) utilizing toroidal edge adjacency.

steps.prompt: Circle the four corners {0, 2, 8, 10} as a single group of 4.

explanation: Cells 0 (0000), 2 (0010), 8 (1000), and 10 (1010) occupy the four corners of the map. Because the top/bottom and left/right borders are adjacent on the Gray-code torus, these 4 cells form a single group. Across all four cells, B=0 and D=0 remain invariant, yielding B'D'.
problems.learningObjective: Exploit toroidal border wrap-around adjacency to group four corner cells into a 2-literal term.

problems.title: Critical don't-care expansion: F = A'D + CD
problems.statement: Minimize F(A,B,C,D) = Σm(1, 3, 7, 11, 15) with don't-cares d(5, 9).

steps.prompt: Form groups incorporating don't-care cell 5 to maximize group size.

explanation: Minterms {3, 7, 11, 15} form a full column where C=1 and D=1 -> CD. For the remaining minterm m1, grouping with m3, m7 and don't-care m5 forms a group of 4 {1, 3, 5, 7} where A=0 and D=1 -> A'D. Don't-care m9 is left unused because it does not further simplify any required minterms. Minimal SOP: A'D + CD.
problems.learningObjective: Selectively include don't-care cells only when they expand group size and reduce term cost.

problems.title: Cyclic core with dual minimal covers (Petrick's Method)
problems.statement: Find all minimal covers for 3-variable cyclic core function F(A,B,C) = Σm(0, 1, 2, 5, 6, 7).

steps.prompt: Find a minimal 3-group cover for the cyclic core.

explanation: All prime implicants are pairs: {0,1}=A'B', {0,2}=A'C', {1,5}=B'C, {2,6}=BC', {5,7}=AC, {6,7}=AB. None is essential because every minterm is covered by exactly two PIs. Petrick's expansion reveals two symmetrical minimal covers of 3 terms: (1) A'B' + AC + BC' and (2) A'C' + AB + B'C.
problems.learningObjective: Resolve cyclic prime implicant charts without essential implicants using Petrick's method and list alternative minimal covers.

problems.title: 5-variable 3D grouping spanning both layers: F = B'D'
problems.statement: Minimize 5-variable function F(A,B,C,D,E) = Σm(0, 1, 4, 5, 16, 17, 20, 21) across layers A=0 and A=1.

steps.prompt: Combine the identical 4-cell groups in Layer 0 (A=0) and Layer 1 (A=1) into a single 8-cell 3D group.

explanation: In Layer 0 (A=0), cells {0, 1, 4, 5} form a 4-cell group B'D'. In Layer 1 (A=1), cells {16, 17, 20, 21} occupy the exact same subgrid positions. Because they are adjacent along the 5th variable dimension A, they combine into an 8-cell group. Variable A is eliminated, yielding B'D'.
problems.learningObjective: Identify cross-layer symmetry in 5-variable K-maps to eliminate the 5th variable across dual 4x4 subgrids.

problems.title: Minimal Product of Sums (POS) grouping: F = (A + C)
problems.statement: Find the minimal POS expression for the 4-variable function whose maxterms are M(0, 1, 4, 5).

steps.prompt: Group the four 0-cells {0, 1, 4, 5} and write the dual sum term.

explanation: To find the minimal POS, group the 0-cells on the map: cells {0, 1, 4, 5}. In these cells, A=0 and C=0. In dual POS form, a literal of 0 is represented uncomplemented: (A + C).
problems.learningObjective: Group 0-cells on a Karnaugh map to obtain simplified Product of Sums expressions with correct dual literal polarities.
